Definition: properly, dangling, i.e. (by implication) weak or thin
BiblicalUsage: The poor are everywhere in Scripture, and this word names the thin, the weak, the dangling ones with nothing to hold onto. Hannah sang that the Lord raises the poor out of the dust and lifts the beggar from the dunghill to sit among princes, and the prophets charge Israel to defend the poor and to give them bread. The remnant God leaves in the midst of Jerusalem is an afflicted and poor people, and they trust in the name of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's heart for the poor is not an afterthought in Scripture; it is one of its loudest themes. I hold that how we treat the poor is how we treat Him, because He has put His own name beside theirs, and the one who gives to the poor lends to the Lord.
